title: Prakrama 1, Sarga 16. The Journey to Gaya
html:
Ancestral rites at the holy places of Gaya; Jagannatha Mishra appears to accept the pinda; love awakens at the footprint of Vishnu; a voice from the sky bids the Lord return home; His ecstasy in Navadvipa; a brief glance ahead — sannyasa, Puri, the South, Mathura; the fruit of hearing

Verse 1

गुरौ स भक्तिं परिदर्शयन्स्वयं
फल्गुषु चक्रे पितृदेवतार्चनम्।
प्रेतादिशृङ्गे पितृपिण्डदानं
ब्रह्माङ्गुलीरेणुयुतेषु कृत्वा॥१॥

gurau sa bhaktiṁ paridarśayansvayaṁ
phalguṣu cakre pitṛdevatārcanam|
pretādiśṛṅge pitṛpiṇḍadānaṁ
brahmāṅgulīreṇuyuteṣu kṛtvā||1||

gurau — towards the guru; sah — He; bhaktim — devotion; paridarshayan — showing; svayam — Himself; phalgushu — at the Phalgu; chakre — performed; pitri-devata-archanam — worship of forefathers and gods; preta-adi-shringe — on the peak of Preta (Pretashila); pitri-pinda-danam — the offering of pinda to the forefathers; brahma-anguli-renu-yuteshu — on (spots) bearing the dust of Brahma's fingers; kritva — having made.

1Himself showing what devotion to the guru should be, He worshipped the forefathers and the gods at the Phalgu, and on the peak of Pretashila, on spots bearing the dust of Brahma's fingers, offered pindas to the forefathers1.

Verse 2

देवान्समभ्यर्च्य ददौ द्विजातये
पितॄन्समुद्दिश्य यथेष्टदक्षिणाम्।
ततोऽवरुह्याशु ययावुदीचीं
पितृक्रियां दक्षिणमानसे च॥२॥

devānsamabhyarcya dadau dvijātaye
pitṝnsamuddiśya yatheṣṭadakṣiṇām|
tato'varuhyāśu yayāvudīcīṁ
pitṛkriyāṁ dakṣiṇamānase ca||2||

devan — the gods; samabhyarchya — having worshipped; dadau — gave; dvijataye — to the brahmana; pitrin — the forefathers; samuddishya — on behalf of; yatha-ishta-dakshinam — as much dakshina as desired; tatah — then; avaruhya — descending; ashu — quickly; yayau — went; udichim — northward; pitri-kriyam — the rite for the forefathers; dakshina-manase — at Dakshina-manasa; cha — and.

2Having worshipped the gods, He gave the brahmanas as much dakshina as they wished on behalf of His forefathers; then He quickly came down and went north. Having performed the ancestral rite at Dakshina-manasa

Verse 3

कृत्वोत्तरे मानससंज्ञके च
ययौ स जिह्वाचपले द्विजान्वितः।
श्राद्धं पितॄणामथ देवतानां
कृत्वा गयामूर्ध्नि जगाम हृष्टः॥३॥

kṛtvottare mānasasaṁjñake ca
yayau sa jihvācapale dvijānvitaḥ|
śrāddhaṁ pitṝṇāmatha devatānāṁ
kṛtvā gayāmūrdhni jagāma hṛṣṭaḥ||3||

kritva — having performed; uttare manasa-samjnake — at the (pond) called Uttara-manasa; cha — and; yayau — went; sah — He; jihvachapale — to Jihvachapala; dvija-anvitah — with the brahmanas; shraddham — the shraddha; pitrinam — to the forefathers; atha — and; devatanam — to the gods; kritva — having performed; gaya-murdhni — to the head of Gaya; jagama — went; hrishtah — joyful.

3and at the (pond) called Uttara-manasa, He went with the brahmanas to Jihvachapala. Having performed there the shraddha for the forefathers and the gods, He went joyfully to the head of Gaya2.

Verse 4

द्विजोत्तमैः षोडशवेदिकायां
चकार पिण्डं पितृकर्मपूर्वकम्।
श्रीमज्जगन्नाथपुरन्दराख्यः
प्रत्यक्षीभूय जगृहे मुदान्वितः॥४॥

dvijottamaiḥ ṣoḍaśavedikāyāṁ
cakāra piṇḍaṁ pitṛkarmapūrvakam|
śrīmajjagannāthapurandarākhyaḥ
pratyakṣībhūya jagṛhe mudānvitaḥ||4||

dvija-uttamaih — with the best of brahmanas; shodasha-vedikayam — at the Sixteen Altars; chakara — made; pindam — the pinda; pitri-karma-purvakam — with the ancestral rite; shrimat-jagannatha-purandara-akhyah — he named Srimad Jagannatha Purandara; pratyakshibhuya — appearing visibly; jagrihe — accepted; muda-anvitah — joyfully.

4At the Sixteen Altars3, together with the best of brahmanas, He performed the ancestral rite and offered the pinda — and Srimad Jagannatha Purandara, appearing visibly, joyfully accepted it.

Verse 5

यथा श्रीरामेण हि दत्तपिण्डो
गृहीत आगम्य तदीयपित्रा।
एवं हि सर्वत्र हरेश्चरित्रं
तथापि दुष्प्राप्यतमं यदेतत्॥५॥

yathā śrīrāmeṇa hi dattapiṇḍo
gṛhīta āgamya tadīyapitrā|
evaṁ hi sarvatra hareścaritraṁ
tathāpi duṣprāpyatamaṁ yadetat||5||

yatha — as; shri-ramena — by Sri Rama; hi — indeed; datta-pindah — the pinda offered; grihitah — was accepted; agamya — coming; tadiya-pitra — by his father; evam — so; hi — indeed; sarvatra — everywhere; hareh — of Hari; charitram — the deeds; tatha api — and yet; dushprapyatamam — most rarely attained; yat — which; etat — this.

5Just so, long ago, the pinda offered by Sri Rama was accepted by His father, who came for it4. Thus Hari's deeds are alike everywhere — and yet this event is the rarest of all.

Verse 6

स विष्णुपद्यां हरिपादचिह्नं
दृष्ट्वातिहृष्टो मनसाब्रवीच्च।
कथं हरेः पादपयोजलक्ष्म-
प्रेमोदयो मे न बभूव दृष्ट्वा॥६॥

sa viṣṇupadyāṁ haripādacihnaṁ
dṛṣṭvātihṛṣṭo manasābravīcca|
kathaṁ hareḥ pādapayojalakṣma-
premodayo me na babhūva dṛṣṭvā||6||

sah — He; vishnupadyam — at the Vishnupada; hari-pada-chihnam — the footprint of Hari; drishtva — seeing; ati-hrishtah — overjoyed; manasa — to Himself; abravit — said; cha — and; katham — why; hareh — of Hari; pada-payoja-lakshma — the marks of the lotus foot; prema-udayah — an awakening of love; me — in Me; na — not; babhuva — has come; drishtva — on seeing.

6Seeing the footprint of Hari at the Vishnupada, He was overjoyed, but said to Himself: "Why, on seeing the marks of Hari's lotus foot, have I felt no awakening of love?"

Verse 7

तस्मिन्क्षणे तस्य बभूव दैवा-
त्सुशीततोयैरभिषेचनं मुहुः।
कम्पोर्ध्वरोमा भगवान्बभूव
प्रेमाम्बुधाराशतधौतवक्षाः॥७॥

tasminkṣaṇe tasya babhūva daivā-
tsuśītatoyairabhiṣecanaṁ muhuḥ|
kampordhvaromā bhagavānbabhūva
premāmbudhārāśatadhautavakṣāḥ||7||

tasmin kshane — at that moment; tasya — its (the footprint's); babhuva — took place; daivat — by providence; su-shita-toyaih — with very cool water; abhishechanam — a bathing; muhuh — again and again; kampa-urdhva-roma — trembling, His hair on end; bhagavan — Bhagavan; babhuva — became; prema-ambu-dhara-shata-dhauta-vakshah — His chest washed by a hundred streams of tears of love.

7At that moment, by providence, the footprint was bathed again and again with very cool water5 — and Bhagavan trembled, His hair stood on end, and His chest was washed by a hundred streams of tears of love.

Verse 8

स विह्वलः कृष्णपदाब्जयुग्म-
प्रेमोत्सवेनाशु विमुक्तसङ्गः।
त्यक्त्वा गयां गन्तुमियेष रम्यां
मधोर्वनं साधुनिषेवितां ताम्॥८॥

sa vihvalaḥ kṛṣṇapadābjayugma-
premotsavenāśu vimuktasaṅgaḥ|
tyaktvā gayāṁ gantumiyeṣa ramyāṁ
madhorvanaṁ sādhuniṣevitāṁ tām||8||

sah — He; vihvalah — beside Himself; krishna-pada-abja-yugma-prema-utsavena — by the festival of love for Krishna's lotus feet; ashu — at once; vimukta-sangah — free of all attachment; tyaktva — leaving; gayam — Gaya; gantum — to go; iyesha — wished; ramyam — lovely; madhoh vanam — to Madhuvana; sadhu-nishevitam — frequented by saints; tam — that.

8Beside Himself with the festival of love for Krishna's lotus feet, at once free of all attachment, He wished to leave Gaya and go to lovely Madhuvana6, frequented by saints.

Verse 9

प्राहाशरीरा नवमेघनिस्वना
वाणी तमाहूय चल स्वमन्दिरम्।
ततः परं कालवशेन देव
मधोर्वनं चान्यदपि स्वचेष्टया॥९॥

prāhāśarīrā navameghanisvanā
vāṇī tamāhūya cala svamandiram|
tataḥ paraṁ kālavaśena deva
madhorvanaṁ cānyadapi svaceṣṭayā||9||

praha — said; asharira — bodiless; nava-megha-nisvana — with a sound like a fresh rain-cloud; vani — a voice; tam — Him; ahuya — calling; chala — go; sva-mandiram — to Your home; tatah param — after that; kala-vashena — in due time; deva — O Lord; madhoh vanam — to Madhuvana; cha — and; anyat api — elsewhere too; sva-cheshtaya — by Your own will.

9Then a bodiless voice, deep as a fresh rain-cloud, called Him and said: "Go to Your home. Afterwards, in due time, O Lord, You will go by Your own will both to Madhuvana and elsewhere.

Verse 10

भवान्हि सर्वेश्वर एष निश्चितः
कर्तुं ह्यकर्तुं च समर्थः सर्वतः।
तथापि भृत्यैर्गदितं च यत्प्रभो
कर्तुं प्रमाणं हि तमर्हसि ध्रुवम्॥१०॥

bhavānhi sarveśvara eṣa niścitaḥ
kartuṁ hyakartuṁ ca samarthaḥ sarvataḥ|
tathāpi bhṛtyairgaditaṁ ca yatprabho
kartuṁ pramāṇaṁ hi tamarhasi dhruvam||10||

bhavan — You; hi — indeed; sarva-ishvarah — the Lord of all; eshah — this; nishchitah — certainly; kartum — to do; hi — indeed; akartum — not to do; cha — and; samarthah — able; sarvatah — in every way; tatha api — even so; bhrityaih — by servants; gaditam — spoken; cha — and; yat — what; prabho — O Lord; kartum — to make; pramanam — true; hi — indeed; tam — that; arhasi — You should; dhruvam — surely.

10You are certainly the Lord of all, able in every way to do or not to do. Yet, O Lord, the word spoken by Your servants You must surely make true."

Verse 11

स इत्थमाकर्ण्य गिरं सुदिव्या-
मागत्य गेहं निजबन्धुभिर्वृतः।
ननाम मातुश्चरणे निपत्य
बभूव हर्षाश्रुविलोचना शची॥११॥

sa itthamākarṇya giraṁ sudivyā-
māgatya gehaṁ nijabandhubhirvṛtaḥ|
nanāma mātuścaraṇe nipatya
babhūva harṣāśruvilocanā śacī||11||

sah — He; ittham — such; akarnya — hearing; giram — words; su-divyam — divine; agatya — coming; geham — home; nija-bandhubhih — by His kinsmen; vritah — surrounded; nanama — bowed; matuh — of His mother; charane — at the feet; nipatya — falling; babhuva — became; harsha-ashru-vilochana — her eyes filled with tears of joy; shachi — Shachi.

11Having heard this divine speech, He came home, surrounded by His kinsmen, and fell at His mother's feet in obeisance; and Shachi's eyes filled with tears of joy.

Verse 12

गृहे वसन्प्रेमविभिन्नधैर्यं
रुदत्यलं रौति मुहुर्मुहुः स्वनैः।
सवेपथुर्गद्गदया गिरा लप-
त्यलं हरे कृष्ण हरे मुदा क्वचित्॥१२॥

gṛhe vasanpremavibhinnadhairyaṁ
rudatyalaṁ rauti muhurmuhuḥ svanaiḥ|
savepathurgadgadayā girā lapa-
tyalaṁ hare kṛṣṇa hare mudā kvacit||12||

grihe — at home; vasan — living; prema-vibhinna-dhairyam — His composure shattered by love; rudati — weeps; alam — abundantly; rauti — cries out; muhuh muhuh — again and again; svanaih — aloud; sa-vepathuh — trembling; gadgadaya gira — in a faltering voice; lapati — calls; alam — much; hare — O Hari; krishna — O Krishna; hare — O Hari; muda — joyfully; kvachit — at times.

12Living at home, His composure shattered by love, He would weep long and cry out loudly again and again, and at times, trembling, He would joyfully call in a faltering voice: "Hari! Krishna! Hari!"

Verse 13

श्रीवासविप्रादिगणैः क्वचिन्नवं
गायत्यलं नृत्यति भावपूर्णः।
नानावतारानुकृतिं वितन्व-
न्रेमे नृलोकाननुशिक्षयंश्च॥१३॥

śrīvāsaviprādigaṇaiḥ kvacinnavaṁ
gāyatyalaṁ nṛtyati bhāvapūrṇaḥ|
nānāvatārānukṛtiṁ vitanva-
nreme nṛlokānanuśikṣayaṁśca||13||

shrivasa-vipra-adi-ganaih — with Srivasa, brahmanas and others; kvachit — at times; navam — anew; gayati — sings; alam — abundantly; nrityati — dances; bhava-purnah — full of feeling; nana-avatara-anukritim — imitation of various avatars; vitanvan — displaying; reme — He delighted; nri-lokan — people; anushikshayan — teaching; cha — and.

13At times, with Srivasa, the brahmanas and others, He sang in new ways and danced, full of feeling, and, imitating various avatars, He took delight in this and taught the people.

Verse 14

न्यासं स चक्रे हरिपादपद्मे
सर्वां क्रियां न्यासिवरो बभूव।
ततोऽगमत्क्षेत्रवरे महात्मभि-
र्वृतो मुकुन्दप्रमुखैर्हरिप्रियैः॥१४॥

nyāsaṁ sa cakre haripādapadme
sarvāṁ kriyāṁ nyāsivaro babhūva|
tato'gamatkṣetravare mahātmabhi-
rvṛto mukundapramukhairharipriyaiḥ||14||

nyasam — renunciation; sah — He; chakre — made; hari-pada-padme — at Hari's lotus feet; sarvam — of every; kriyam — action; nyasi-varah — the best of sannyasis; babhuva — became; tatah — then; agamat — went; kshetra-vare — to the best of kshetras; maha-atmabhih — by great souls; vritah — surrounded; mukunda-pramukhaih — headed by Mukunda; hari-priyaih — dear to Hari.

14He laid down all action at Hari's lotus feet and became the best of sannyasis. Then, surrounded by great souls headed by Mukunda, dear to Hari, He went to the best of kshetras7

Verse 15

ददर्श देवं पुरुषोत्तमेश्वरं
चिरं चिरानन्दसुखातिसत्सुखम्।
लब्ध्वागमद्राघवदेवनिर्मितं
सेतुं पथि प्राज्ञजनैः स साधुभिः॥१५॥

dadarśa devaṁ puruṣottameśvaraṁ
ciraṁ cirānandasukhātisatsukham|
labdhvāgamadrāghavadevanirmitaṁ
setuṁ pathi prājñajanaiḥ sa sādhubhiḥ||15||

dadarsha — saw; devam — the Lord; purushottama-ishvaram — the Lord of Purushottama; chiram — for long; chira-ananda-sukha-ati-sat-sukham — the true bliss surpassing everlasting joy and happiness; labdhva — having attained; agamat — went; raghava-deva-nirmitam — built by Lord Raghava; setum — to the bridge; pathi — on the road; prajna-janaih — with wise men; sah — He; sadhubhih — saintly.

15and long beheld the Lord, the Master of Purushottama — the true bliss surpassing everlasting joy and happiness. Having attained this, He went with wise and saintly men along the road to the bridge built by Lord Raghava8.

Verse 16

तत्र स्थितान्सप्ततमालवृक्षा-
नालिङ्ग्य चक्रे मुहुरेव रोदनम्।
ततः समागत्य ददर्श कूर्मे
स कूर्मरूपं जगदीश्वरं प्रभुः॥१६॥

tatra sthitānsaptatamālavṛkṣā-
nāliṅgya cakre muhureva rodanam|
tataḥ samāgatya dadarśa kūrme
sa kūrmarūpaṁ jagadīśvaraṁ prabhuḥ||16||

tatra — there; sthitan — standing; sapta-tamala-vrikshan — the seven tamala trees; alingya — embracing; chakre — gave way; muhuh — long; eva — indeed; rodanam — to weeping; tatah — then; samagatya — coming; dadarsha — saw; kurme — at Kurma; sah — He; kurma-rupam — in the form of a tortoise; jagat-ishvaram — the Lord of the world; prabhuh — Prabhu.

16Embracing the seven tamala trees9 that stand there, He wept long. Then Prabhu came to Kurma and saw the Lord of the world in the form of a tortoise10.

Verse 17

तदागमच्छ्रीपुरुषोत्तमाख्ये
क्षेत्रे जगन्नाथमुखं ददर्श।
कियद्दिनं तत्र निवासमच्युतो
विधाय यातो मथुरां मधुद्विषः॥१७॥

tadāgamacchrīpuruṣottamākhye
kṣetre jagannāthamukhaṁ dadarśa|
kiyaddinaṁ tatra nivāsamacyuto
vidhāya yāto mathurāṁ madhudviṣaḥ||17||

tada — then; agamat — He came; shri-purushottama-akhye kshetre — to the kshetra called Sri Purushottama; jagannatha-mukham — the face of Jagannatha; dadarsha — saw; kiyat-dinam — for some days; tatra — there; nivasam — stay; achyutah — Achyuta; vidhaya — having made; yatah — went; mathuram — to Mathura; madhu-dvishah — of the Enemy of Madhu.

17Then He came back to the kshetra called Sri Purushottama and saw the face of Jagannatha. Having stayed there some days, Achyuta went to Mathura, the city of the Enemy of Madhu.

Verse 18

पादाब्जचिह्नैः समलङ्कृतां स्थलीं
रुरोद सम्प्राप्य लुठन्क्षितौ भृशम्।
कियद्दिनं तत्र स्थितो जगद्गुरुः
प्रेमामृतास्वादनमात्र उत्सुकः॥१८॥

pādābjacihnaiḥ samalaṅkṛtāṁ sthalīṁ
ruroda samprāpya luṭhankṣitau bhṛśam|
kiyaddinaṁ tatra sthito jagadguruḥ
premāmṛtāsvādanamātra utsukaḥ||18||

pada-abja-chihnaih — with the marks of lotus feet; samalankritam — adorned; sthalim — the land; ruroda — He wept; samprapya — reaching; luthan — rolling; kshitau — on the ground; bhrisham — vehemently; kiyat-dinam — some days; tatra — there; sthitah — stayed; jagat-guruh — the Teacher of the world; prema-amrita-asvadana-matre — for the tasting of the nectar of love alone; utsukah — eager.

18Reaching the land adorned with the marks of (Krishna's) lotus feet, the Teacher of the world wept, rolling vehemently on the ground, and stayed there some days, eager only to taste the nectar of love.

Verse 19

इति स मधुपुरीं प्रभुर्वितन्व-
न्परमसुखं सहसा जगाम हर्षात्।
पुनरनुपदमेव साधुसङ्गा-
त्परमपदं पुरुषोत्तमप्रदीव्यम्॥१९॥

iti sa madhupurīṁ prabhurvitanva-
nparamasukhaṁ sahasā jagāma harṣāt|
punaranupadameva sādhusaṅgā-
tparamapadaṁ puruṣottamapradīvyam||19||

iti — thus; sah — He; madhu-purim — in Madhupuri; prabhuh — Prabhu; vitanvan — spreading; parama-sukham — supreme bliss; sahasa — suddenly; jagama — went; harshat — in joy; punah — again; anupadam — step by step; eva — indeed; sadhu-sangat — in the company of saints; parama-padam — to the supreme abode; purushottama-pradivyam — the playground of Purushottama.

19Thus, having spread supreme bliss in Madhupuri, Prabhu suddenly left in joy and again, step by step, in the company of saints, came to the supreme abode — the playground of Purushottama.

Verse 20

श्रुत्वा च तीर्थस्य विधिक्रियां हरे-
र्लभेद्गयातीर्थफलं महत्तमम्।
देहावसाने विमलां गतिं नरः
श्रद्धान्वितो गच्छति पूर्णलालसः॥२०॥

śrutvā ca tīrthasya vidhikriyāṁ hare-
rlabhedgayātīrthaphalaṁ mahattamam|
dehāvasāne vimalāṁ gatiṁ naraḥ
śraddhānvito gacchati pūrṇalālasaḥ||20||

shrutva — hearing; cha — and; tirthasya — of the holy place; vidhi-kriyam — the performance of rites; hareh — of Hari; labhet — one gains; gaya-tirtha-phalam — the fruit of pilgrimage to Gaya; mahattamam — the greatest; deha-avasane — at the end of the body; vimalam — pure; gatim — destination; narah — a man; shraddha-anvitah — endowed with faith; gachchhati — reaches; purna-lalasah — with full longing.

20Whoever hears how Hari performed the rites at the holy place gains the greatest fruit of pilgrimage to Gaya; and a man full of faith and complete longing reaches, at the end of the body, a pure destination.

Thus ends the sixteenth sarga, "The Journey to Gaya" (Gaya-gamana), of the first prakrama of the great poem "Sri Krishna-chaitanya-charitamrita." Thus the first prakrama is complete.

✦

Notes

  1. The Phalgu is the sacred river of Gaya; Pretashila is a hill near Gaya where pindas (balls of rice) are offered to the forefathers. Its stones, by local tradition, bear the marks of Brahma's fingers. The reading "on the peak of Pretashila" is conjectural.
  2. Dakshina-manasa, Uttara-manasa and Jihvachapala (Jihvalola) are holy places of Gaya where shraddha is performed. "The head of Gaya" is the spot on the head of the asura Gaya on which Vishnu placed His foot; the shrine of the Vishnupada stands there.
  3. The Sixteen Altars (Shodasha-vedi) are the place of pinda offerings by the Vishnupada temple.
  4. Rama's father is Dasharatha.
  5. Literally "its": apparently the footprint of Vishnu; it may also be understood that the Lord Himself was drenched with cool water.
  6. Madhuvana, the forest of Madhu, is the region of Mathura (Vraja).
  7. Verses 14–19 briefly anticipate events described in detail in the following prakramas: the sannyasa, the life in Puri (the kshetra of Purushottama), and the pilgrimages to the South and to Mathura.
  8. Raghava is Rama; the bridge (Setubandha) is the bridge to Lanka built by Rama.
  9. The tamala is a tree with dark bark whose colour recalls Krishna.
  10. Kurma is Kurma-kshetra (Srikurmam) in the South, where Vishnu is worshipped in the form of the Tortoise.
